st.headline: Japan’s benchmark 10-year bond yield reaches 3% level for first time in 30 years
st.teaser: The five-year rate is at a record high, and the two-year yield is at a 31-year peak.
fullText: TOKYO – Japan’s benchmark bond yield hit the 3 per cent level for the first time since September 1996 on Sept 1 , highlighting how inflation, fiscal concerns and shifting monetary policy are reshaping a market long defined by low interest rates.

With the Middle East crisis stoking inflation fears globally and pressure on the Bank of Japan to accelerate rate hikes, yields have jumped to historic levels across the Japanese government bond curve.

The 10-year JGB yield has more than tripled in two years. On the shorter end, the five-year rate is at a record high, and the two-year yield is at a 31-year peak as markets priced in a near certainty the BOJ will raise interest rates at its meeting in September.
Inflationary pressures and the yen, languishing near a four-decade low, have exerted pressure on the BOJ to speed up rate hikes.
The central bank has faced criticism at home and abroad that it was “behind the curve” in normalising monetary policy, which includes a gradual drawdown of its massive JGB holdings.

Japan’s bond sell-off has drawn attention because the country’s heavy debt burden makes it especially vulnerable to rising borrowing costs. Demand at a 10-year JGB auction in August was the weakest in a year.
Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi has pushed an investment-led growth path targeting strategic industries since taking office in October.
That spending along with planned tax cuts have stoked concerns that Japan could worsen its precarious financial position, with debt exceeding 200 per cent of gross domestic product.
Japan is not alone in seeing stress in its bond market.

With no end in sight for the US-Iran conflict and elevated oil prices, bond yields across the United States, Germany and France jumped to multi-year highs of late on rising expectations for inflation and central bank tightening. REUTERS

cna.headline: Osaka brings style and steel for winning start to US Open
cna.teaser: Osaka brings style and steel for winning start to US Open
fullText: NEW YORK, Aug 31 : Naomi Osaka unveiled another bold Grand Slam walk-on outfit at the U.S. Open on Monday before the two-time champion battled to a 7-6(6) 7-6(3) victory over unseeded Russian Anastasia Zakharova to reach the second round.

Osaka has been the fashion highlight of this year's majors and entered Arthur Ashe Stadium in a hooded tunic featuring patchwork-style panels adorned with press clippings from past tournament appearances and a billowing white tulle train.
At Wimbledon, she paid tribute to her Japanese heritage with a kimono-inspired ensemble featuring a traditional kanzashi hair ornament before changing into a white Nike playing kit.
At Roland Garros, she arrived in a black Kevin Germanier skirt and competed in a layered yellow, brown and gold outfit inspired by the Eiffel Tower's nighttime sparkle.

Competing at Flushing Meadows in an Allen Iverson-inspired outfit, the four-time Grand Slam champion looked set for a straightforward victory after racing into a 4-1 lead, only for world number 101 Zakharova to force a tiebreak.
"It's my tribute to Iverson," Osaka said of the NBA Hall of Famer. "I really like him a lot.
"Nike said basketball, so I said 'you want basketball, I'll give you basketball'. I like expressing myself through clothes and I'm glad you guys appreciate it."
Osaka showed her battling qualities to win the tiebreak before being taken to another in the second set, where she held her nerve to close out the victory.
"I would say it took everything (to win)," Osaka said as the clock approached 12:30 a.m. on Tuesday.
"I have no idea what time it is. Thanks for staying," she told fans. "I'm grateful to be able to play on this court again.

"I just told myself to not have any regrets. I wanted to come out and compete. I haven't played since Toronto, so I was a little rusty. I get nervous in the first rounds. I want to do well and show you guys new outfits."
The 13th seed, champion at Flushing Meadows in 2018 and 2020, takes on Czech Republic's Katerina Siniakova in the second round.

economistArticle.title: The Sunshine State’s Star: Can Miami’s Boom Last?
paras: Over the past few years, Miami has undergone a stunning economic metamorphosis. Once known primarily as a playground for tourists and retirees, the city has rapidly evolved into a magnet for high finance and tech startups. This dramatic shift is not a mere stroke of fortune; rather, it is the result of a deliberate alignment of political incentives and an influx of private capital seeking refuge from high-tax jurisdictions.

Wall Street heavyweights and Silicon Valley venture capitalists have flocked to South Florida, bringing with them billions of dollars in assets under management. This influx has spurred a commercial real estate boom, with glossy new skyscrapers reshaping the downtown skyline. Local officials have capitalised on this momentum, offering business-friendly policies and heavily marketing the city's enviable climate and lifestyle.

However, this breakneck growth has also brought significant challenges. The most pressing of these is housing affordability. As wealthy newcomers bid up home prices, local residents are increasingly priced out of the market. The city’s infrastructure, from transit systems to drainage networks, is also under immense strain, exacerbated by the existential threat of rising sea levels due to climate change.

To sustain its newfound status, Miami must address these deep-seated structural issues. Simply attracting capital is no longer enough; the local government must now ensure that the benefits of the boom are distributed more equitably. Investing in public transportation and flood mitigation infrastructure will be crucial to securing the city's long-term viability as a global hub.

Ultimately, Miami’s rise demonstrates the power of combining business-friendly governance with a high quality of life. Yet, whether it can retain its position as America’s newest economic powerhouse depends on how it manages the externalities of its own success. The coming decade will test whether Miami can transition from a speculative boomtown to a resilient global metropolis.
economistArticle.cn:
在过去的几年里，迈阿密经历了一场令人瞩目的经济蜕变。这座曾经主要被视为游客和退休人员游乐场的城市，已迅速演变为吸引高端金融和科技初创企业的磁石。这种戏剧性的转变并非纯粹的运气，而是政治激励举措与旨在逃避高税收管辖区的私人资本涌入刻意结合的结果。

华尔街巨头和硅谷风险投资家纷纷涌向南佛罗里达，随之而来的是数以十亿计的管理资产。这一涌入刺激了商业地产的繁荣，崭新光滑的摩天大楼重塑了市中心的天际线。当地官员利用这一势头，提供了有利于商业的政策，并大力推广该市令人羡慕的气候和生活方式。

然而，这种极快的增长也带来了重大的挑战。其中最紧迫的是住房负担能力问题。随着富裕的新移民推高房价，当地居民越来越被排挤出市场。该市的基础设施，从交通系统到排水网络，也承受着巨大的压力，而由于气候变化导致的海平面上升这一生存威胁更是加剧了这一状况。

为了维持其新获得的地位，迈阿密必须解决这些根深蒂固的结构性问题。仅仅吸引资本已经不够了，当地政府现在必须确保繁荣带来的红利能够更公平地分配。投资公共交通和防洪缓解基础设施，对于确保该市作为全球枢纽的长期可行性至关重要。

归根结底，迈阿密的崛起展示了将亲商治理与高质量生活相结合的力量。然而，它能否保持其作为美国最新经济强国的地位，取决于它如何管理自身成功所带来的外部性。未来十年将测试迈阿密能否从一个投机性的繁荣城镇转型为一个有韧性的全球大都市。
